items.followUp: What is meant by an anabolic metabolic pathway?

rubric.why: A metabolic pathway consists of a sequence of connected reactions.
rubric.description: Defines a metabolic pathway as a series of linked chemical reactions.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the reactions as a series or sequence.

rubric.why: Identifies enzyme control or the link between successive reactions.
rubric.description: States that reactions are enzyme-catalysed, or that the product of one reaction becomes the substrate for the next.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for either enzyme catalysis or the product-to-substrate link.

modelAnswer: A metabolic pathway is a series of linked chemical reactions in a cell.
Each reaction is catalysed by an enzyme, and the product of one reaction may become the substrate for the next.

items.followUp: What causes atherosclerosis, and how can it affect blood flow?

rubric.why: Identifies the general change to artery walls in arteriosclerosis.
rubric.description: Defines arteriosclerosis as hardening or thickening of artery walls, with loss of elasticity.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing hardening, thickening, or loss of elasticity.

rubric.why: Identifies the fatty plaque build-up specific to atherosclerosis.
rubric.description: Defines atherosclerosis as the build-up of fatty or cholesterol-rich plaques in artery walls.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying fatty deposits or plaques in artery walls.

modelAnswer: Arteriosclerosis is the general hardening and thickening of artery walls, which causes them to lose elasticity.
Atherosclerosis is a type of arteriosclerosis in which fatty or cholesterol-rich plaques build up in the inner walls of arteries.
